Let me look at both plus how resources use them.So `core/streaming.ts` is a file, not a directory. Let's fetch it.Now let's look at how resources (chat, responses, beta.assistants, etc.) invoke streaming — search for `Stream.fromSSEResponse` usage and `stream: true` handling across resources.Excellent, this gives clear API surface for chat completions: `create()` with `stream: true`, `runTools()`, and `.stream()`. Now let's check `responses.ts` (Responses API) and `beta/assistants` / `beta/threads` for their streaming methods.Now let's check `beta/threads` (Assistants API) for streaming methods, and confirm `AssistantStream.ts`.I have enough evidence now to compose a complete answer.I now have complete evidence to answer.

## Streaming implementation in `openai/openai-node`

### Core low-level implementation
**`src/core/streaming.ts`** (re-exported for back-compat via the now-deprecated `src/streaming.ts`) is where raw HTTP streaming lives:
- `class Stream<Item>` — the async-iterable wrapper the SDK returns for any streamed API call. Provides `[Symbol.asyncIterator]`, `.tee()`, `.toReadableStream()`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — parses a `fetch` `Response` as Server-Sent-Events (via the internal `_iterSSEMessages` generator + `SSEDecoder`/`LineDecoder`), yielding parsed JSON chunks. Used for Chat Completions, Responses, Assistants/Runs, and transcription streaming.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — builds a `Stream` from a plain newline-delimited `ReadableStream`; used internally by the higher-level helper streams (`ChatCompletionStream`, `AssistantStream`) once they've done their own request plumbing.

### Where streaming is triggered generically
**`src/internal/parse.ts`**, function `defaultParseResponse()` — this is the single chokepoint all API calls pass through. If `FinalRequestOptions.stream` is true, it calls either a custom `options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (if the resource specified one) or falls back to `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` from `core/streaming.ts`. This is *the* place that "routes into" streaming — every `.create()`-style method that sets `stream: true` on its request options ends up here.

### Higher-level, ergonomic stream wrappers (`src/lib/`)
Built on top of the core `Stream`/SSE plumbing, exposing an `EventEmitter`-style API (`src/lib/EventStream.ts` is the shared base class):
- **`src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts`** — `ChatCompletionStream` (extends `AbstractChatCompletionRunner`), accumulates chunks into a full `ChatCompletion`, emits `content`, `chunk`, `message`, etc.
- **`src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts`** / **`AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts`** / **`ChatCompletionRunner.ts`** — power the tool-calling "runner" helpers.
- **`src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts`** — `ResponseStream`, with `ResponseAccumulator.ts` (accumulates `ResponseStreamEvent`s into a final `Response`) and `EventTypes.ts`.
- **`src/lib/AssistantStream.ts`** — `AssistantStream` for the (beta) Assistants/Runs streaming API.

### Public API methods that route into streaming
| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({ stream: true })` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79` | sets `stream: body.stream ?? false` on the request → `defaultParseResponse` → `Stream.fromSSEResponse` → `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(body)` | same file, `:221-225` | calls `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion(...)` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(body)` when `body.stream` | same file, `:196-215` | delegates to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools(...)` |
| `client.responses.create({ stream: true })` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-122` | same `stream:` flag → core `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve({ stream: true })` | same file, `:137-168` | same pattern (retrieving a streamed in-progress response) |
| `client.responses.stream(body)` | same file, `:201-205` | calls `ResponseStream.createResponse(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create(threadId, { stream: true })` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-82` | core `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / deprecated `createAndStream(...)` | same file, `:161-233` | `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs({ stream: true })` / `.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file, `:246-299` | core `Stream` or `AssistantStream.createToolAssistantStream(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({ stream: true })` / `.createAndRunStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:143-183` | core `Stream` or `AssistantStream.createThreadAssistantStream(...)` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({ stream: true })` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:43-62` | core `Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>` (SSE); explicitly not supported for `whisper-1` per doc comment |

Every one of these methods just forwards `stream: <bool>` into `this._client.post(...)`/`.get(...)`, and the actual branching to SSE parsing happens centrally in `defaultParseResponse` (`src/internal/parse.ts`), which calls into `src/core/streaming.ts`.

### What I did not verify
- I did not check the **Realtime API** (`src/realtime/`, `src/resources/realtime/`) in depth — that uses WebSocket-based streaming, a materially different transport from the SSE/`ReadableStream` mechanism described above, and was out of scope for this pass.
- I did not inspect `src/client.ts`'s `post`/`get`/request-building code to trace exactly how the `stream` option becomes `FinalRequestOptions.stream` (I confirmed the consuming side in `parse.ts`, not the option-plumbing side in the base client).
- I read files via the GitHub Contents API against the default branch; I did not check git blame/history or verify these are unchanged as of a specific commit SHA.
- I did not exhaustively check every resource file (e.g., `containers`, `evals`, `videos`) for possible additional streaming methods beyond the ones surfaced by grep — the ones listed above are the ones I found evidence for.
